title: Materialism and Empirio-Criticism
author: V. I. Lenin
desc: Defensa del materialismo filosófico contra el idealismo disfrazado de ciencia.
tesis: Lenin defiende el materialismo filosófico contra los 'empiriocriticistas' que introducían idealismo disfrazado de ciencia en el marxismo ruso. La materia existe independientemente de nuestra conciencia — negarla es volver al idealismo. Es una defensa combativa de la epistemología materialista: la realidad objetiva existe, podemos conocerla, y la ciencia es el método para hacerlo.
ideas: La materia existe independientemente de nuestra conciencia — el idealismo, en cualquier versión, niega esta verdad fundamental.
La filosofía no es neutral: toda corriente filosófica sirve a intereses de clase.
El materialismo es la única filosofía compatible con la ciencia y la práctica revolucionaria.
contexto: Escrito en 1908, publicado en 1909, durante el período de reacción que siguió a la derrota de la revolución de 1905. Algunos marxistas rusos (Bogdánov, Lunacharski) se volcaron hacia la filosofía idealista de Mach y Avenarius. Lenin los atacó porque consideraba que abandonar el materialismo era abandonar la base filosófica de la revolución.

conexiones.razon: Engels estableció el materialismo; Lenin lo defiende contra nuevas formas de idealismo.
La Dialéctica de la Naturaleza y Materialismo y Empiriocriticismo defienden el mismo proyecto.

quotes.text: Matter is a philosophical category denoting the objective reality which is given to man by his sensations, and which is copied, photographed and reflected by our sensations, while existing independently of them.

tl: Berkeley publishes Treatise on Human Knowledge

The work of Bishop George Berkeley, published in 1710 under the title Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge begins with the following argument. This was written in 1710, fourteen years before the birth of Immanuel Kant.
Diderot writes the sentient piano dialogue
We are instruments endowed with sensation and memory. Our senses are so many keys upon which surrounding nature strikes and which often strike upon themselves. That was written in 1769.
pp. 23 to 26
Marx writes to Feuerbach against Schelling
As far back as 1843, when Marx was only becoming Marx, the founder of socialism as a science, the founder of modern materialism, Marx pointed out with amazing clarity the basic trends in philosophy.
Marx fixes practice as criterion of truth

We have seen that Marx in 1845 and Engels in 1888 and 1892 placed the criterion of practice at the basis of the materialist theory of knowledge. The dispute over the reality of thinking isolated from practice is a purely scholastic question.
Dietzgen formulates motion without matter is unthinkable

J. Dietzgen in 1869, in his The Nature of the Workings of the Human Mind, expressed the same idea as Engels. The transformation of matter into force is here for Cohen the most important triumph of idealism.
Mach declares task of science is sensations

The task of science, Mach wrote in 1872, can only be to determine the laws of connection of ideas, to discover the laws of connection of sensations, and to explain the laws of connection between sensations and ideas.
Avenarius publishes Philosophie als Denken der Welt

We saw that Mach in 1872 and Avenarius in 1876 held a purely idealist view; for them the world is our sensation. Avenarius idealism emerges so clearly in his work of 1876 that Avenarius himself in 1891 was obliged to admit it.
pp. 35 to 40
Mach publishes The Science of Mechanics

In 1883 Machs Mechanics appeared, and in the preface to the first edition Mach refers to Avenarius Prolegomena, and greets his ideas as being very close to his own philosophy. Sensations are not symbols of things.
pp. 27 to 40
Engels publishes Ludwig Feuerbach

The foreword to Ludwig Feuerbach, dated February 1888. These words of Engels refer to German professorial philosophy in general. Engels followed the new developments in philosophy is evident from Ludwig Feuerbach.
pp. 50 and 318
Chernyshevsky writes preface censored by tsar

Chernyshevsky is the only really great Russian writer who, from the fifties until 1888, was able to keep on the level of an integral philosophical materialism and who spurned the wretched nonsense of the neo-Kantians.
Avenarius admits idealist starting point

In the introduction to The Human Concept of the World Avenarius says: He who has read my first systematic work, Philosophie, etc., will at once presume that I would have attempted to treat the problems from the idealist standpoint.
Engels writes last preface to Anti-Dühring

Schulze, a follower of Hume, described in 1792 the relation between the question of space and time and the question of an objective reality outside us just as the materialist Engels described it in 1894.
Bogdanov still defends materialist view
A. Bogdanov, The Fundamental Elements of the Historical Outlook on Nature. St. Petersburg, 1899, p. 216. In the nine years from 1899 to 1908, Bogdanov has gone through four stages.
pp. 37 to 38
Russian revolution and rise of Machist deviation

A religious-philosophical trend hostile to Marxism, which arose in the period of reaction among a section of the Party intellectuals who had deserted from Marxism after the defeat of the revolution of 1905 to 1907.
Bogdanov circle publishes Studies in Philosophy of Marxism

Studies in the Philosophy of Marxism (St. Petersburg, 1908), a symposium by Bazarov, Bogdanov, Lunacharsky, Berman, Helfond, Yushkevich and Suvorov. How certain Marxists in 1908 and certain idealists in 1710 refuted materialism.
pp. 7 to 10
Lenin publishes Materialism and Empirio-Criticism in Moscow

The book Materialism and Empirio-criticism. Critical Comments on a Reactionary Philosophy was written by Lenin during February to October 1908 in Geneva and London. It was published in Moscow in May 1909 by the Zveno Publishers.
